Marcus —

Thanks for taking this. Quick context: BlueNova is planning to move our customer-facing generation endpoints to a Dedicated capacity model (want predictable latency & data isolation). High level workload: real-time chat + summary generation for documents. A few asks up front so your sizing math matches our expectations: 

- Typical prompt+history -> ~150 tokens in, average generation 110 tokens (we see a median of 120 tokens total per request).
- Expected steady-state: 18 requests/sec across our US region during business hours; expected 3x peak bursts (up to ~54 rps) for product launches.
- P95 latency target (end-to-end generation): <= 350 ms for single-turn chat (excluding network), and p99 should not exceed 650 ms.
- We care about graceful degradation: if Dedicated capacity is saturated we'd like automatic fallback to hosted model with clear degradation profile.

Attached is a small CSV with recent RPS/time breakdowns. Can you send a tokens/sec estimate, which GPU SKUs you'd map to (H100/H800/A100), and proposed slab sizing + recommended safety multiplier? Also please confirm KV/prefix caching assumptions — we currently expect a 20% cache hit rate for repeated prompts.

Thanks — if it helps, happy to do a 30m call next week.

Sara Lin
Head of ML Platform, BlueNova

Folks — did a quick back-of-envelope and then populated the workbook (attached). Summary of assumptions and numbers: 

Assumptions (model & perf):
- Baseline model: 7B decoder with some quantization (we assume a 4-bit quantized path similar to our ver. 2 profiles).
- Measured generation throughput (approx):
  - H100 (latest gen): ~9,000 tokens/sec sustained for short-context generation 
  - A100: ~5,500 tokens/sec sustained 
  - H800 (cloud SKU): ~7,200 tokens/sec sustained
- Latency mapping: p95 token-streaming latency (end-to-end) approximations — on H100 single-shot 120-token generation ~= 220-280 ms depending on KV/cache warmness; A100 closer to 350-420 ms at same load.
- KV cache: 20% hit rate reduces effective tokens/sec by 20% (i.e., multiply needed throughput by 0.8).

Workload math (peak):
- Median tokens/request: 120 (customer).
- Peak rps: 54 => raw peak tokens/sec = 120 * 54 = 6,480 t/s.
- Effective tokens/sec after 20% cache hits = 0.8 * 6,480 = 5,184 t/s.

GPU sizing (recommended slabs):
- Option A (latency-priority): 1 x H100 slab (~9k t/s) covers peak with ~1.7x headroom. This comfortably meets p95 <= 350ms in our benchmarks. Recommend this if p95 is non-negotiable.
- Option B (cost-balanced): 1 x H800 slab (~7.2k t/s) covers peak with ~1.39x headroom; p95 borderline during sustained peak but should pass with autoscaling/burst lanes.
- Option C (cost-minimal): 2 x A100 smaller slabs (each ~5.5k t/s) — two A100s give ~11k t/s combined but operationally more complex; single A100 falls short.

Safety multipliers and deployment pattern:
- Base reserved slab: size to cover steady-state + 1.3x safety. Steady-state tokens/sec = 120 * 18 = 2,160; after cache => 1,728 t/s. With 1.3x safety => ~2,246 t/s. So minimal reserved slab could be an A100 if you only size for steady-state.
- Peak / launch events: we recommend a burst slab (on-demand or pre-warmed H100) sized to absorb 3x spikes. For simplicity, recommend base: 1 x H800 reserved (7.2k), burst: 1 x H100 on pre-warm for launches. 
- Conservative commercial offer: reserved H800 + ability to pre-warm an H100 for 24-72 hours during launches. If their procurement prefers a single SKU, go H100 reserved.

Operational notes:
- Tail latency is sensitive to cold KV cache — recommend a brief warm-up plan and a policy to prioritise prefix caching for in-app hot paths.
- Recommend circuit-breaker thresholds: at 85% slab utilization trigger autoscale or redirect a percentage of traffic to hosted fallback (we can define the % per degradation tier).

I've attached blue-nova_throughput_workbook.xlsx with the per-SKU tab calculations and an ops playbook tab with suggested thresholds.

— Ben

Sara — thanks for the details and the CSV. Apologies for the short delay; we wanted to validate numbers internally and attach a small workbook that lays out the slab math and an ops playbook. TL;DR recommendations: 

1) Recommended primary slab (latency-balanced): reserved H800 slab (1 x H800) + pre-warmed H100 available for launches. Rationale: H800 covers sustained peaks with ~1.4x headroom after caching; H100 pre-warm gives extra headroom for launches without committing to H100 full-time.

2) If P95 is a hard SLA requirement: reserve 1 x H100. Our benchmarks show single-turn 120-token generations at p95 <= 350ms on H100 with the quantized profile we discussed.

3) Safety & fallbacks:
- Base safety multiplier: 1.3x for steady-state sizing (we used this to size reserved slab).
- Launch safety multiplier: plan for 1.6x (or pre-warm H100 for the 24-72 hour window).
- Fallback policy: at 85% slab utilisation we trigger (a) pre-warmed burst H100, (b) if unavailable, gradual percentage-based redirect to hosted API with clearly documented latency tiers (we will provide standard wording for the contract).

4) KV caching: we assumed 20% effective cache hit rate in the workbook. If you can confirm higher cache hits on hot prefixes, committed slab can be reduced proportionally.

5) Next steps:
- We attached blue-nova_throughput_workbook.xlsx (per-SKU tabs + ops thresholds) and sizing-diagram.png (logical slab/burst flow). Please review; Ben can walk through the workbook with your infra team.
- Commercial: Kimberly & Neha will follow up with two proposals: (a) H800 reserved + H100 pre-warm add-on pricing, (b) H100 reserved (SLA-backed) pricing.
- Suggested call: 30m on Tue/Wed next week to confirm assumptions and sign off on a pilot reservation window.

If you want, I'll propose times and Ben can run a live perf demo on a short-history 7B quantized profile to show p95 behavior.
